s: A company is migrating an application to AWS. It wants to use fully managed services as much as possible during the migration The company needs to store large, important documents within the application with the following requirements 1 The data must be highly durable and available 2. The data must always be encrypted at rest and in transit. 3 The encryption key must be managed by the company and rotated periodically Which of the following solutions should the solutions architect recommend?
o: Deploy the storage gateway to AWS in file gateway mode Use Amazon EBS volume encryption using an AWS KMS key to encrypt the storage gateway volumes
Use Amazon S3 with a bucket policy to enforce HTTPS for connections to the bucket and to enforce server-side encryption and AWS KMS for object encryption.
Use Amazon DynamoDB with SSL to connect to DynamoDB Use an AWS KMS key to encrypt DynamoDB objects at rest.
Deploy instances with Amazon EBS volumes attached to store this data Use EBS volume encryption using an AWS KMS key to encrypt the data.

w.y: Amazon S3 is fully managed and built for high durability and availability for large objects. A bucket policy can deny requests where aws:SecureTransport is false, which enforces encryption in transit, and can require SSE-KMS. SSE-KMS with a customer managed key lets the company control and rotate the key.

o.A: File Gateway is a hybrid appliance for on-premises access, not a fully managed store in AWS, and it stores data in S3 anyway.
o.B: Correct: S3 with a bucket policy enforcing HTTPS and SSE-KMS meets durability, encryption at rest and in transit, and key control.
o.C: DynamoDB items are limited to 400 KB, so it is unsuitable for large documents.
o.D: Self-managed EBS on EC2 is not fully managed, and one volume in one AZ is less durable and available than S3.
